Zoologist Nightingale. Rose Petals in a Sunlit Church.
Embark on a parfume journey
1 day ago - 10/11/2026
1 3

Zoologist Nightingale. Rose Petals in a Sunlit Church.

Oh, what a wonderful brand – Zoologist! I’ll never tire of singing its praises, browsing the collection roughly every six months and re-discovering what I like and what I don’t. I’m definitely keen to build up my own collection of full-size Zoologist bottles and I’m well on my way to doing so.

Now, Nightingale.

It’s all about roses. Rose soap, a bath scented with rose oil or sprinkled with rose petals. There’s jasmine, lily of the valley and tuberose scattered all around, with a little pink pepper adding a crisp, slightly fizzy, tart freshness. And then there’s incense. Just the thinnest thread of frankincense, barely noticeable in the background, blending so beautifully with the rose. I imagine a statue of the Virgin Mary in a Catholic church, surrounded by rose petals. The church is almost empty, flooded with sunlight, with very little decoration and plenty of air.

There’s something wonderfully pure and peaceful about the whole scene. As the fragrance develops, the flowers gradually give way to rose and frankincense. And oh my God, what beautiful frankincense! Especially together with that rose. Despite its rich floral character, Nightingale is actually a quiet fragrance that stays quite close to the skin.

I picture a beautiful young woman, glowing with the energy of youth, tenderness and a thirst for life, dreaminess and elusive beauty, arriving for Sunday Mass. She’s just had a shower and still smells of rose soap. Inside the church, the air carries that delicate scent of frankincense. The freshness of her rose soap and the incense mingle almost effortlessly. Everything feels light and airy, as though the sunlight itself were carrying the scent of rose oil and frankincense through the church.

Absolutely beautiful. Pure, tender, bright. Feminine.
